title: Cohort priority tree and unstick procedures (personal rollout notes)
content:
Quick personal scratchpad for selecting cohorts during model flips and a short, usable 'unstick' playbook for when traffic/clients get trapped on an old variant. Meant to be an operational cheat-sheet + checklist I can copy into runbooks.

Background/context:
- We keep getting requests for partial model rollouts by client segments (paid tier, EU clients, internal QA, API token groups). Need deterministic selection tree so SREs and account teams can reason about coverage and edge cases (backfills, SDK caching, proxies).
- Recent incident (INC-2025-01): SDK caching + client affinity caused ~40% of a midmarket cohort to remain on the deprecated variant after a partial flip. We need a short procedure to detect + unstick without full rollback.

Goals for this doc:
- Provide a reproducible cohort priority decision tree for progressive rollout
- Spell out quick detection queries and the minimum-viable unstick steps
- Outline simulation/offline dry-run checklist so we don't repeat surprises

Cohort priority tree (first-pass rules)
1) Explicit client opt-in cohorts (highest priority)
   - customers who signed up for beta via support ticket/feature-flag include-list
   - ALWAYS honor explicit flag overrides set via /feature_flags API
2) Account tier (paid flag)
   - paid > trial > free. Paid accounts should get preferential rollout when gating for revenue-impacting models
3) Region/Compliance group
   - region flags (EU users) — ensure model variant meets compliance before including
4) Tagged client attributes (token metadata)
   - e.g., integration: "voice-sdk", "low-latency". Some integrations require older model variants until upstream SDK changes land
5) Random sample window (progressive ramp)
   - use deterministic hashing on client_id -> [0,1) and compare to fraction threshold. Keep seed/versioning in telemetry
6) Shadow/audit cohorts (observe-only)
   - mirrored traffic for metrics only; not counted toward target fraction

Decision notes:
- Deterministic hashing seed needs to be pinned to the rollout id (rollout-YYYYMMDD-x) so we can reproduce cohorts later.
- If multiple rules match, choose the highest-priority rule (lower number above). Example: paid EU client with tag "voice-sdk" -> honor explicit opt-in first, then account tier.

Key telemetry (queries to run during canary)
- p95_latency_by_variant (last 10m, 1m gran)
- error_rate_5xx_by_variant (last 10m)
- token_cost_delta_by_variant (token burn per request average)
- model_quality_baselines: rerank_score_drop, hallucination_rate_estimate (for eval hooks)
- client_affinity_leak: fraction of requests from client_A still hitting old_variant after traffic > 30% for client

Sample alert conditions (soft)
- p95(delta) > 150ms for >5m => investigate
- error_rate_variant_A > 1% absolute and at least 2x baseline
- client_affinity_leak > 20% for a single client after 10m of traffic change

Unstick playbook (fast) — minimal steps to get stranded clients back on correct variant without global rollback
- Preconditions: have ability to flip flags per-client and to flush SDK edge caches (if available). Have rollout id and target seed.
- Target: move affected client(s) through deterministic rehash or bypass caching layer to force new route.

1) Confirm symptoms
   - run client_affinity_leak query for the client_id(s). Confirm that traffic fraction hitting old_variant > 20% despite global route change.
   - check edge cache TTLs (via edge-cache dashboard or request headers)
2) Temporary manual reassign via control plane
   - If client on include-list: toggle explicit flag to force new_variant. (API call: POST /feature_flags/{flag}/override {client_id, variant})
   - If no per-client flag: create a temporary override cohort with higher priority and add client_id(s) to it
3) Probe and validate
   - run a small synthetic request from the client's IP/region (curl with x-client-id) to confirm routing changes.
   - verify telemetry: p95 for that client moves to expected variant metrics and served_variant header changes
4) Edge cache flush (if needed)
   - If the SDK or CDN is caching route decisions, trigger cache invalidation for the client token (invalidate key: client_id|route)
   - If invalidation is slow, use a bypass header toggle for the client for N minutes (X-Bypass-Route: true)
5) Warm rebalancing window
   - Keep override in place for 5–15 minutes while monitoring. If stable, remove override to restore algorithmic routing (the client will rehash deterministically now)

Full rollback vs unstick guidance
- Rollback if: global error spike or quality regression affecting >20% of traffic or outage-level (S0/S1). Faster to rollback when runbooks tested.
- Unstick if: isolated cohort/client affinity issues, caches, or SDK pinning causing misrouting. Unstick less disruptive and keeps rollout progress for rest of traffic.

Offline simulation checklist (pre-canary)
- Replay 24h of sampled traffic through the new routing logic in a staging cluster. Compare cohort assignment distribution to expected fractions.
- Simulate SDK cache TTLs: run synthetic clients with cached route header and ensure deterministic rehash catches them after TTL expire.
- Run cost projection: token burn ratio for new_variant vs old_variant at 1k/10k/100k qps
- Test client override API: add/remove client in 10s and validate route changes within 60s

Playful flow (if visual helps):
- client_id -> check explicit override? -> yes -> honor override
                   -> no -> check opt-in list? -> yes -> include
- else -> apply account-tier rule -> region rules -> tag rules -> deterministic-hash sample

Operational tips / gotchas (notes to self)
- SDKs that cache 'served_variant' header are the most common cause of long-lived affinity. Need an SDK header change rollout whenever we change routing semantics.
- Proxy infra (customer gateways) that reuse connection pools across token swaps can also pin traffic. If possible, force connection drain for affected clients during warm windows.
- Keep a small set of always-recoverable test clients (internal corp tokens) to validate unstick steps without involving a customer

Short command snippets
- Query client affinity leak (example):
  SELECT served_variant, count(1) as cnt FROM requests
  WHERE client_id = 'C12345' AND timestamp > now() - interval '15 minutes'
  GROUP BY served_variant ORDER BY cnt desc;

- Apply per-client override (control-plane curl):
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
    -d '{"client_id":"C12345","variant":"new-llm-v2","expires_at":"2025-02-02T02:30:00Z"}' \
    https://control-plane.internal/feature_flags/variant_override

Open questions / follow-ups
- Should we expose per-client override in console or keep it API-only? (I lean API-only for auditability but console convenience for SREs)
- Do we need SDK version check in the cohort selection tree? (maybe — add as a tag rule)
- Add a TTL meta-field for overrides so they don't become permanent by accident.

Copy-out checklist for an actual incident (short):
[ ] Identify affected client(s) and confirm affinity leak >20%
[ ] Try per-client override via API
[ ] Run synthetic probe from client region
[ ] Invalidate edge cache / enable bypass header if needed
[ ] Monitor for 15 minutes, remove override when stable
[ ] File postmortem link and assign follow-ups (SDK changes, console feature)

Notes to self: keep this as the canonical minimal unstick playbook. The longer runbook can reference these steps. When time, convert the SQL samples into saved dashboard queries and bake a one-click 'unstick' in runbook-runner (follow-up ticket created).

-- end --
